outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no posting has given an unconditional asymptotic, with the Keating–Snaith leading constant, for the 2k-th moment of |ζ(1/2+it)| for any k ≥ 3; the window holds unconditional lower bounds of the conjectured order (sixth moment with constant 34.4 against a conjectured 42, Durkan–Page, June 2026; further unconditional lower bounds for 2k = 10 to 22 in the same paper; a sixth- and eighth-moment lower-bound paper by Page, Journal of Number Theory 280 (2026), whose first posting I could not locate), plus analogues for derivatives, L-function families and fractional moments, and AI-involved zeta results that concern zeros or zero-free regions rather than the integral.
problem_asks: The bullet, read from its statement alone: (a) asymptotics, as T tends to infinity, of an integral involving the Riemann zeta function. The bullet does not write the integral or its parameters out, and the bullet's only link is to the Riemann zeta function article. (b) Read as the conjecture of that name, the integral is I_k(T) = ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt, and the question is its behaviour for every k; the bullet names no particular k, and the literature states the conjecture for natural k and, in Keating–Snaith's own framing, for real k with Re k > −1/2. (c) The leading-order claim: I_k(T) ~ a_k g_k/(k²)! · T (log T)^{k²}, where a_k is an arithmetic factor (an Euler product) and g_k a random-matrix constant given by Barnes G-function values, g_k = (k²)! G(k+1)²/G(2k+1). This leading constant is what the name points to; the bullet itself asserts only 'asymptotics'. (d) Lower-order terms (the Conrey–Farmer–Keating–Rubinstein–Snaith recipe) are a stronger conjecture and are not visible in the bullet's wording. Whether (c) is the question or only (a) is a reading the judging pass should confirm; I have taken the integral and the constant as the object because that is what the name denotes.

events.what_happened: J. P. Keating and N. C. Snaith, ‘Random matrix theory and ζ(1/2+it)’, Communications in Mathematical Physics 214 (2000), 57–89. They model the value distribution of ζ near height T by the characteristic polynomial of a large Circular Unitary Ensemble matrix, compute its moments exactly, and conjecture the leading asymptotic for ∫|ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt (the conjecture this bullet is named after). This is the origin of the conjecture, not a proof. The Bristol research-portal record was read; the Bristol PDF was fetched but returned binary data and its text could not be read.
events.revisions: No arXiv identifier was found in searches. The Bristol copy records receipt on 20 December 1999 and acceptance on 24 March 2000 (from a search summary of the PDF, not read directly). The 1998 Vienna RH-conference announcement is reported in a search summary of a Wikipedia biography, not opened.
events.delivers: No theorem: it states the conjecture that the leading term of ∫_0^T|ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt is a_k g_k/(k²)! · T(log T)^{k²}, with the random-matrix constant g_k supplied by the CUE computation and the arithmetic factor a_k supplied separately.
events.remains: Everything: no unconditional or conditional proof is attributed to this paper; only k = 1 and k = 2 were known at the time (see the Hardy–Littlewood and Ingham events).
events.direction: Conjecture; cuts toward the form of the asymptotic that later results (Ng 2016, Ng–Shen–Wong, Durkan–Page) are checked against.

events.what_happened: Hardy and Littlewood's 1918 asymptotic for the second moment: ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|² dt ~ T log T (the k = 1 case). Known here only through the 2016 arXiv abstract of Ng, which states the 1918 result; the 1918 paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Full leading asymptotic for k = 1: the integral of the second power is asymptotic to T log T, matching a_1 g_1 / 1! = 1 in the conjectured form.
events.remains: All k other than 1 within the conjecture's family: k = 2 is Ingham (1926); k ≥ 3 remains open unconditionally.
events.direction: Confirms the conjectured order and constant at k = 1; consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Ingham's 1926 asymptotic for the fourth moment (the k = 2 case): ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|⁴ dt is a quartic polynomial in log T times T, plus an error term. Stated in the 2016 Ng abstract (that Ingham evaluated the fourth moment in 1926) and in the 2025 Durkan–Palojärvi–Trudgian introduction (which writes it as T·P_4(log T) + E_2(T) and cites Heath-Brown 1979). The leading constant 1/(2π²) appears only in a search summary of a survey, not in a source I opened, so I do not rely on it.
events.delivers: Leading asymptotic of order T(log T)⁴ for k = 2, matching the conjectured form at k = 2 (conjectured exponent k² = 4).
events.remains: k ≠ 2; in particular every k ≥ 3, where no asymptotic was known at the frozen revision.
events.direction: Confirms the conjectured order at k = 2; consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: D. R. Heath-Brown, ‘The fourth power moment of the Riemann zeta function’, J. London Math. Soc. (3) 38 (1979), 385–422. As cited in the 2025 Durkan–Palojärvi–Trudgian introduction, Heath-Brown proved the fourth-moment formula with error term E_2(T) ≪ T^{7/8+ε}. The 1979 paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Refines the k = 2 case: full asymptotic with lower-order terms and error T^{7/8+ε}. Reported in the cited paper as giving explicit lower-order coefficients; I did not read those formulas.
events.remains: Every k ≠ 2, and for k = 2 nothing beyond the stated error term.
events.direction: Refines the k = 2 case, consistent with the conjecture; no bearing on k ≥ 3.

events.what_happened: J. B. Conrey and S. M. Gonek, ‘High moments of the Riemann zeta-function’, arXiv math/9902162 (AIM report 1999-2), first submitted 1 February 1999. A general heuristic method that would produce the conjectured formula for every even moment; applied to the sixth power it reproduces the Conrey–Ghosh conjecture, and for the eighth power it gives a new conjecture. These are conjectures, not proofs. The published version (Duke Math. J., 2001) was seen only in search summaries; a search summary also reports that their sixth- and eighth-moment estimates agree with the Keating–Snaith predictions. I could not read that comparison in the source (the AIM PDF and the Duke page returned binary or an interstitial).
events.revisions: Single arXiv version (v1, 1 Feb 1999). Duke Mathematical Journal 2001 per search summary.
events.delivers: No theorem. Conjectured leading terms for k = 3 (sixth power, agreeing with Conrey–Ghosh) and k = 4 (eighth power, new), derived heuristically; the search summary reports agreement with the Keating–Snaith constants.
events.remains: A proof for k = 3 and k = 4 (later addressed conditionally by Ng 2016 for k = 3 and by Ng–Shen–Wong for k = 4); every k ≥ 5.
events.doubts: The method is heuristic. Search summaries of the Conrey–Keating series (not opened) report that the long-Dirichlet-polynomial method fails at the tenth moment and needs extra terms; that is a limit on the method, not a demonstrated error in the eighth-moment prediction.
events.direction: Heuristic conjectures for k = 3 and k = 4 that cut toward the Keating–Snaith constants.

events.what_happened: A. J. Harper, ‘Sharp conditional bounds for moments of the Riemann zeta function’, arXiv 1305.4618, submitted 20 May 2013. Under the Riemann Hypothesis, the integral of |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} over [T, 2T] is at most a constant (depending on k) times T(log T)^{k²}, for every fixed k ≥ 0 and large T. No journal reference is listed on the arXiv page.
events.revisions: Single version (v1) listed.
events.delivers: Conditional on RH: an upper bound of the conjectured order T(log T)^{k²} for every fixed k ≥ 0, on [T, 2T]. It does not determine the leading constant, which is the part the conjecture predicts.
events.remains: The leading constant for every k; unconditional status.
events.direction: Upper bound of the conjectured order with an undetermined constant; consistent with the conjecture, does not settle it.

events.what_happened: Thi Altenschmidt, ‘Sharp upper bound for the sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line’, arXiv 2304.07581, first submitted 15 April 2023. The abstract (read as a paraphrase; the tool would not reproduce it verbatim) bounds a Laplace-type transform of |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2β} and states the consequence ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|⁶ dt ≪_ε T^{1+ε}.
events.revisions: v2 17 Aug 2023; v3 28 Aug 2023; v4 14 Sep 2023 (the version read).
events.delivers: Upper bound only, with a power of T and no power of log T: ∫_0^T|ζ|⁶ ≪ T^{1+ε}. The expected order is T(log T)⁹, so this bound is much weaker in its logarithmic dependence. Whether it is unconditional is not stated in the abstract I read.
events.remains: The asymptotic and the correct order T(log T)⁹ for the sixth moment; the bound is not sharp in the sense the conjecture needs.
events.time_since_posted: about 3.5 years; no later engagement found in searches
events.doubts: The title says ‘sharp’, but the consequence stated in the paraphrase is T^{1+ε} with no logarithm, far from the conjectured T(log T)⁹. I read only the abstract paraphrase; the full text was not read, so I cannot say which quantity the sharpness refers to.
events.direction: Upper bound that does not reach the conjectured order for k = 3.

events.what_happened: Nathan Ng, ‘The sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function and ternary additive divisor sums’, arXiv 1610.04977, first submitted 17 October 2016. It shows that a conjectural formula for a family of ternary additive divisor sums implies an asymptotic formula with power-saving error for the sixth moment of ζ on the critical line. It makes rigorous a heuristic of Conrey and Gonek, and gives evidence for a shifted-moment conjecture of CFKRS. Final version appears in Discrete Analysis (2021:6, 60 pp.) according to the arXiv comments.
events.revisions: v2 3 Mar 2020; v3 6 Jul 2021 (the final version, per arXiv comments); Discrete Analysis 2021:6.
events.delivers: Conditional on an unproven conjecture about a family of ternary additive divisor sums: an asymptotic for the sixth moment (k = 3) with power-saving error term. The conjecture's exact form is in the paper, not in the abstract I read.
events.remains: The unconditional sixth-moment asymptotic; the ternary additive divisor conjecture itself; all k ≥ 4 (the eighth moment is the next event).

checked_by.qualification: Journal that accepted the final version after peer review
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the final version as Discrete Analysis 2021:6, 60 pp.

events.direction: Asymptotic for k = 3 conditional on a divisor-sum conjecture; cuts toward the conjectured form and constant for the sixth moment, conditionally.

events.what_happened: Nathan Ng, Quanli Shen and Peng-Jie Wong, ‘The eighth moment of the Riemann zeta function’, arXiv 2204.13891, submitted 29 April 2022 (single version, 56 pages). Under the Riemann Hypothesis and a quaternary additive divisor conjecture (Conjecture 1 in the paper), the paper proves the leading-term asymptotic for the eighth moment: I_4(T) ~ (24024·a_4/16!) · T(log T)^{16}. The authors say the argument ‘only wins by an ε’ and that no lower-order terms are obtained. Published in the Journal of the European Mathematical Society 28 (2026), no. 10, pp. 4175–4237, according to a search listing (the ems.press page was not opened).
events.revisions: Single arXiv version (v1). JEMS 28 (2026), no. 10, pp. 4175–4237 per search listing.
events.delivers: Conditional on RH and Conjecture 1 (the quaternary additive divisor conjecture, stated for a smoothed sum with uniform range 1 ≤ |r| ≪ X^{1−ε′}): the leading asymptotic for the eighth moment (k = 4), with the Keating–Snaith constant form. I checked the constant by hand: g_4 = 16!·G(5)²/G(9) = 24024, so 24024·a_4/16! = a_4 g_4/(4²)!.
events.remains: The unconditional eighth-moment asymptotic; lower-order terms; the quaternary additive divisor conjecture; every k ≥ 5 (the paper treats only the eighth power).

checked_by.who: Journal of the European Mathematical Society
checked_by.what_they_did: Published as JEMS 28 (2026), no. 10, pp. 4175–4237 (per search listing; ems.press page not opened)

events.doubts: The paper's own statement (read from the ar5iv HTML) that Conjecture 1 currently has no numerical confirmations; the result is only as strong as that unproven hypothesis. No specific error or retraction was found.
events.direction: Asymptotic for k = 4 conditional on RH and an additive divisor conjecture; the leading constant matches the Keating–Snaith form; cuts toward the conjecture, conditionally.

events.what_happened: Christopher Hughes and Andrew Pearce-Crump, ‘Moments of derivatives of the Riemann zeta function: Characteristic polynomials and the hybrid formula’, arXiv 2406.08121, v1 submitted 12 June 2024. Conjectures (not proofs) for moments of mixed derivatives of ζ evaluated at the nontrivial zeros, reached through CUE characteristic polynomials and the Gonek–Hughes–Keating hybrid model. Analogue: derivatives at zeros, not the integral over t.
events.revisions: v2 9 Sep 2025. The v2 comments say the paper is superseded, one method of proof was removed, and the remaining results were split between arXiv 2509.07788 and 2509.07792. The listing reads 'now withdrawn by Andrew Pearce-Crump' (as read through a tool summary).
events.delivers: Conjectures for moments of derivatives at zeros (under RH, as the authors' framework assumes; the abstract read does not state this). Not an asymptotic for ∫|ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet: a different quantity (values at zeros of derivatives) and no proof.
events.doubts: The v2 comments say a method of proof was removed and the paper is superseded, so the v1 claims are not all standing.

withdrawn.what: v2 listing reads 'now withdrawn by Andrew Pearce-Crump'; v2 comments say superseded, one proof method removed, results split into 2509.07788 and 2509.07792. The exact status (paper withdrawn or version withdrawn) was not confirmed from the arXiv page itself.

events.direction: Analogue (derivatives at zeros); conjectural; does not bear on the integral's asymptotic.

events.what_happened: Christopher Hughes and Andrew Pearce-Crump, ‘Integer moments of the derivatives of the Riemann zeta function’, arXiv 2509.07792, submitted 9 September 2025. A conjectured full asymptotic expansion for a product of zeta functions evaluated at the nontrivial zeros, with shifts; differentiated to give conjectures for integer moments of mixed derivatives. Derived from random matrix theory and the Ratios Conjecture of Conrey, Farmer and Zirnbauer. Conjectural only.
events.revisions: Single version (v1) listed.
events.delivers: Conjectures for integer moments of mixed derivatives of ζ at the nontrivial zeros. Not a theorem and not a statement about the integral over t.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet.
events.direction: Analogue (derivatives at zeros); conjectural; no bearing on the integral's asymptotic.

events.what_happened: Benjamin Durkan, Neea Palojärvi and Tim Trudgian, ‘The error term of the fourth moment of the Riemann zeta-function’, arXiv 2506.16766, first submitted 20 June 2025. They reduce the powers of log T in the known bounds for the error term E_2(T) of the fourth moment, and in the integral of E_2(t)² over [0,T], and obtain logarithmic improvements in upper bounds for ∫|ζ|^{2k} for 8 ≤ k ≤ 12; the explicit example stated is ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^{12} dt ≪ T²(log T)^{15}.
events.revisions: v2 revised 4 Oct 2026 (per tool reading of the listing).
events.delivers: Upper bounds only: improved log powers in the error term for k = 2 and in upper bounds for 2k = 8 to 12 (e.g. the 12th power ≪ T²(log T)^{15}). The power of T (T²) is far from the conjectured order T(log T)^{k²}, which for 2k = 12 gives exponent 36. No asymptotic is stated for any k ≥ 3, and the abstract read does not say whether the bounds are unconditional.
events.remains: The asymptotic for k ≥ 3; the correct order of magnitude for the moments in question.
events.direction: Upper bounds with improved logarithms that do not reach the conjectured order in T; neutral for the asymptotic.

events.what_happened: Hua Lin and Peng-Jie Wong, ‘Towards Keating–Snaith’s conjecture for cubic Hecke L-functions over the Eisenstein field’, arXiv 2511.08783, submitted 11 November 2025. A conditional lower bound, under GRH, toward the Keating–Snaith prediction for central values of L-functions in a thin family of cubic Hecke L-functions over Q(ω). Uses twisted estimates for the one-level density of these L-functions; builds on Radziwiłł–Soundararajan.
events.revisions: Single version (v1) listed.
events.delivers: Conditional on GRH: a lower bound of the conjectured type for central values in one thin family of cubic Hecke L-functions over the Eisenstein field. Explicitly about L-function central values, not the zeta integral.
events.remains: The zeta integral ∫|ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k}dt for every k, and the asymptotic constant.
events.direction: Analogue (central values in an L-function family, conditional on GRH); cuts toward the family version of the conjecture, not the zeta integral.

events.what_happened: Hung M. Bui, Richard R. Hall and Martin Subira Jorge, ‘Amplified Fourth Moment of the Riemann Zeta-Function and Applications’, arXiv 2511.14415, submitted 18 November 2025. An asymptotic for the fourth moment of ζ times the fourth power of an amplifier of length T^ϑ, with applications to large gaps between zeros (the paper reports Λ > 2.64 with ϑ = 0.1249 in the text read) and to lower bounds for moments. Its bibliography cites Page's unconditional sixth- and eighth-moment lower bounds (J. Number Theory 280 (2026)).
events.revisions: Single version (v1) listed.
events.delivers: Asymptotic for an amplified (twisted) fourth moment, i.e. k = 2 with an amplifier. The bullet's k = 2 case is already known, so this is a different integrand. Its bearing is through the amplifier technique and applications, not through a new k.
events.remains: The untwisted sixth and higher moments; the Keating–Snaith constant for k ≥ 3.
events.direction: Analogue (amplified fourth moment, k = 2); not an advance on the bullet's k range.

events.what_happened: T. Page, ‘Unconditional lower bounds for the sixth and eighth moments of the Riemann zeta function’, Journal of Number Theory 280 (2026), pp. 318–369, as cited in reference [19] of Bui–Hall–Subira Jorge (arXiv 2511.14415). I could not locate the paper on arXiv or in journal listings in this session, and I did not read its text. The Durkan–Page introduction cites a Page bound with constant 0.419 for a derivative moment; I did not establish whether that is the same paper.
events.revisions: Not located. The citing paper of 18 Nov 2025 already refers to it as existing, so the first public posting is on or before that date. Whether it predates 26 January 2024 is unknown.
events.delivers: As described by a citing paper only: unconditional lower bounds of the conjectured order for the sixth and eighth moments of ζ(1/2+it). Constants and the exact integral are unknown to me.
events.remains: Per the citing description, the asymptotic with constant for these moments; the constants are not stated in anything I read.

checked_by.what_they_did: Listed as published, vol. 280 (2026), pp. 318–369, by a citing paper; I did not verify the journal record

events.doubts: I have only second-hand descriptions of this paper; its first posting, its constants and its exact hypotheses are unverified.
events.direction: Per citing papers: unconditional lower bounds of the conjectured order for k = 3 and k = 4; not an asymptotic with constant.

events.what_happened: Louis-Pierre Arguin and Nathan Creighton, ‘Lower bounds for the large deviations and moments of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line’, arXiv 2603.01711, submitted 2 March 2026. An unconditional lower bound on the critical line for real large deviations of order V ~ α log log T (α > 0), and, per the authors as summarised, another proof of the sharpest known unconditional lower bounds for fractional moments.
events.revisions: Single version (v1).
events.delivers: Unconditional lower bounds for fractional moments and for large deviations. The large-deviation bound matches a previously proved upper bound for 0 < α < 2 (abstract read). Restricted to the fractional-moment and large-deviation range; no asymptotic for integer 2k.
events.remains: The asymptotic for integer k ≥ 3 and the Keating–Snaith constant; the leading constant for fractional k.
events.direction: Unconditional lower bounds of the conjectured order in the fractional range; cuts toward the conjecture there, no bearing on integer k ≥ 3.

events.what_happened: Zikang Dong, Weijia Wang and Hao Zhang, ‘Lower bounds for high moments of zeta sums’, arXiv 2506.09334, submitted 11 June 2025 (v2 25 Aug 2026). Unconditional lower bounds for high moments of the partial sums Σ_{n≤x} n^{it}, which is a sum over n rather than an integral of |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} over t.
events.delivers: Lower bounds for moments of a different quantity (partial sums of n^{it}). Discounted: not the integral over t of |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k}.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet.
events.direction: Neighbouring quantity; no bearing on the integral's asymptotic.

events.what_happened: Didier Lesesvre and Ade Irma Suriajaya, ‘A connection between low-lying zeros and central values of L-functions’, arXiv 2605.12688, submitted 12 May 2026. Explicit conditional lower bounds toward the Keating–Snaith conjecture for the distribution of central values of L-function families, conditional on partial results toward the Rudnick–Sarnak density conjecture. The page describes the Keating–Snaith conjecture as concerning the distribution of central values, not moments of ζ on the line.
events.revisions: v1 (12 May 2026) is the version listed.
events.delivers: Conditional lower bounds toward the distribution-of-central-values form of the Keating–Snaith prediction, for L-function families, conditional on partial one-level density results. Not a statement about ∫|ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k}dt.
events.remains: The zeta integral for every k and its asymptotic constant.
events.direction: Analogue (distribution of central values in L-function families); conditional; cuts toward the family version of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Benjamin Durkan and Timothy Page, ‘Amplified moments of the Riemann zeta function’, arXiv 2606.27323, v1 submitted 25 June 2026, v2 5 August 2026. Main results read from the abstract and introduction: asymptotic formulae for two-piece amplified second and fourth moments; unconditional effective lower bounds for several joint moments, including Theorem 1, ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|⁶ dt ≥ (34.4+o(1)) c_3 T(log T)⁹ (c_3 = a_3/9!), compared with the Keating–Snaith prediction 42c_3 T(log T)⁹; Theorem 10, unconditional lower bounds of the same type for the 2k-th moments with k = 5 to 11, with the constant for k = 8 (16th power) given as 139.258…; and an improvement of some Soundararajan lower bounds without the Lindelöf hypothesis.
events.revisions: v1 25 Jun 2026; v2 5 Aug 2026 (current).
events.delivers: Unconditional lower bound for the sixth moment of the conjectured order T(log T)⁹ with leading constant 34.4 against the conjectured 42 (34.4/42 ≈ 0.82, my arithmetic). Per the tool's reading of Theorem 10, unconditional lower bounds of the conjectured order for 2k = 10 to 22; the 8th power (k = 4) is not in that range. Restricted to lower bounds on [0, T]; it gives no asymptotic and no upper bound for these moments. Theorem 1 is a bound, not the asymptotic.
events.remains: The sixth-moment asymptotic with the Keating–Snaith constant (the gap 34.4 → 42); the eighth moment (via Page's paper or otherwise); every upper bound and lower-order term; the full asymptotic for all k ≥ 5.
events.direction: Lower bound of the conjectured order with a constant below the conjectured one; cuts toward the conjecture, not an asymptotic.

events.what_happened: Anthropic’s research post ‘Claude has improved on a longstanding lower bound for the fraction of zeros of the Riemann zeta function that satisfy the Riemann hypothesis’ (dated 10 August 2026 per the page, updated 13 August). An unreleased research version of Claude raised the known lower bound on the proportion of nontrivial zeros on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%. The post says the Riemann hypothesis itself is not proved and that Claude’s techniques are not expected to prove it. It does not discuss moments of ζ, Keating or Snaith.
events.revisions: Page updated 13 Aug 2026 with a revised version of Claude’s paper (per the tool reading of the page). Tech Insider gives 5 October 2026 as the publication date; see disputes.
events.delivers: A zeros result: raises the proven proportion of zeros on the critical line (simple-zero and critical-line bounds in the paper's framing). Not about moments, the integral, or the Keating–Snaith constant.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet.

events.what_happened: Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman, ‘More than two thirds of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line’, arXiv 2608.13637, v1 13 August 2026, v2 19 August 2026. Claims an unconditional proof that at least two-thirds of nontrivial zeros, counted with multiplicity, are simple and on the critical line, and at least five-sixths are distinct; constants 0.6725 and 0.8362 via a Montgomery–Taylor window; extends to primitive Dirichlet L-functions. The Comments field credits the proof to Claude (Anthropic) and says the authors verified it; the abstract says it is formally verified in Lean 4.
events.delivers: Zeros: unconditional bounds on the proportion of simple and critical-line zeros (67.25% simple on the line; 83.62% distinct), and on Dirichlet L-function zeros. Not about moments or the integral.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet.
events.doubts: The authors are Anthropic mathematicians who, per the Anthropic post, validated the Claude argument; the verification is therefore not independent of the developer. No outside reading is recorded in this session.
events.direction: Zeros: partial result on RH-type statements; not the integral.

systems.name: Claude (Anthropic)
systems.what_it_did: Per the arXiv comments field: discovered the proof autonomously; the authors say they verified and communicated it. Discounted: zeros, not moments.

events.what_happened: Youness Lamzouri, ‘A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line’, arXiv 2609.02882, v1 2 September 2026, v2 8 September 2026. Single-author unconditional proof that over 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line, and at least 83.62% are distinct, plus two further estimates. The method replaces a finite-dimensional matrix framework with a Hilbert-space inequality and uses Montgomery’s pair correlation theorem (unconditional form of Baluyot, Goldston, Suriajaya and Turnage-Butterbaugh). The abstract says an internal research version of Claude produced an earlier proof of the simple-zero and distinct-zero bounds, verified by Alpöge and Furman; this paper’s argument is by Lamzouri and the two extra estimates are not in the Claude paper.
events.revisions: v2 8 Sep 2026 (current).
events.delivers: Zeros: unconditional simple and distinct zero proportions (67.25%, 83.62%) and two further estimates (88.76% simple-or-critical; average 83.62%). Not about moments or the integral.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet.

events.what_happened: OpenAI released 722 AI-generated mathematical manuscripts (372 families) on GitHub on 6 October 2026, produced ‘the vast majority’ by an unreleased internal OpenAI model. Family 003, ‘The quasi-Riemann hypothesis’, claims no zeros of the Riemann zeta function, Dirichlet L-functions or finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3) with Re s > 7/8; a companion claims the 11/12 region; a further result excludes Landau–Siegel zeros with a Lean scope restriction to 1 − c/log q < β < 1. The repository README lists the zeta zero-free regions among exceptions to the fixed procedure. I scanned all families in the raw CONTENTS.md by title and summary: none concerns moments of ζ, Keating–Snaith, or random matrix moments.
events.revisions: A press report (8 Oct 2026) says three manuscripts were retracted and 719 remain; I could not confirm this in the repository. Scientific American (8 Oct 2026) says some results were retracted after outside scientists found mistakes; the README read does not mention retractions.
events.delivers: Zeros and zero-free regions for ζ, Dirichlet and Hecke L-functions (Re s > 7/8, with a companion 11/12 claim) and Siegel-zero exclusion. Not moments, the integral, or the Keating–Snaith constant.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet.

disputes.summary: Anthropic’s riemann-zeta post is dated 10 August 2026 (updated 13 August) in the page and in Wikipedia’s AI list, but Tech Insider gives 5 October 2026 as the publication date. Unresolved.

The 67.2% / 67.25% critical-line zero bound is claimed by Anthropic’s Claude (post 10 Aug 2026; Alpöge–Furman arXiv 13 Aug 2026) and again by Lamzouri (arXiv 2 Sep 2026), who describes his argument as new and the Claude argument as technically intricate. The record does not settle who first established that figure. Zeros only; no bearing on the moments.

Conflicting reports on who checked the Claude zero proof. The Anthropic post names its own mathematicians (Alpöge, Furman) and two outside experts (Conrey, Goldston) with no published assessment. A Trans-N blog (not opened) says Lamzouri reported no errors; Wikipedia’s AI list says Lamzouri ‘considered it correct’; a DEV Community article (not opened) says the claim is uncorroborated. Lamzouri’s abstract makes no statement about error-checking by himself, beyond attributing the verification to Alpöge and Furman.
A search summary attributed AxiomProver formal certificates to arXiv 2609.02882 (Lamzouri). The fetched abstract page does not mention AxiomProver, and I did not read the full text. Unresolved.

OpenAI’s 722-manuscript release: a press report says three manuscripts were retracted (719 remain) and Scientific American says some results were retracted after outside mistakes were found. The README read does not mention retractions. Unresolved.

Page’s sixth- and eighth-moment lower-bound paper (J. Number Theory 280, 2026) is cited as existing by arXiv 2511.14415 but was not located in searches; its first posting date, constants and content are unverified. Durkan–Page (2606.27323) cites a Page bound with constant 0.419 for a derivative moment; whether this is the same paper is not established.

summary: The problem is the Wikipedia bullet ‘Keating–Snaith conjecture concerning the asymptotics of an integral involving the Riemann zeta function’ (Analytic number theory; its only link is the Riemann zeta article). The bullet does not write the integral out; I read it as the conjecture of that name, the leading asymptotic of ∫_0^T|ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k}dt, with the constant a_k g_k/(k²)! (see problem_asks). Status at the frozen revision: the order and constant are proved for k = 1 (Hardy–Littlewood 1918) and k = 2 (Ingham 1926; Heath-Brown 1979 with error term); conditional leading-term asymptotics exist for k = 3 (Ng 2016, on an unproven ternary additive divisor conjecture) and k = 4 (Ng–Shen–Wong, arXiv April 2022, on RH and a quaternary additive divisor conjecture, whose constant I checked against the Barnes-G formula: g_4 = 24024); Harper (2013, under RH) gives upper bounds of the conjectured order for all k ≥ 0 without the constant. In the window the main items are: (1) Durkan–Page (arXiv 2606.27323, v1 25 June 2026), an unconditional lower bound ∫_0^T|ζ|⁶ ≥ (34.4+o(1))c_3 T(log T)⁹ against the conjectured 42c_3 (I checked 42 = g_3), i.e. the right order with about 82% of the constant; Theorem 10, read through a garbled source, gives the same type of unconditional bound for 2k = 10 to 22; the source gives M_k(T) as the integral of |ζ|^{2k}, so the ‘M₈’ line with exponent 64 is the 16th power, not the eighth. (2) Page, J. Number Theory 280 (2026), reportedly unconditional lower bounds for the sixth and eighth moments; I could not locate its first posting or read it, and I know of it only through citations, so its date relative to the window is unknown. (3) Arguin–Creighton (2 March 2026), unconditional bounds in the fractional-moment and large-deviation range, reaffirming known bounds. Neighbouring analogues and near-misses are recorded as discounted events: Bui–Hall–Subira Jorge (amplified fourth moment, Nov 2025), Lin–Wong (cubic Hecke central values, Nov 2025), Lesesvre–Suriajaya (central-value distributions, May 2026), Hughes–Pearce-Crump (derivatives at zeros, 2024 and 2025, the 2024 version marked withdrawn/superseded), Durkan–Palojärvi–Trudgian (log-power upper bounds for the error term and for 8 ≤ k ≤ 12, June 2025) and Dong–Wang–Zhang (partial sums of n^{it}). Whether (1) and (2) count as progress on the asymptotic is the judging question: they bound the named integral from below at the conjectured order for k = 3 (and, per Theorem 10, for larger k), but no asymptotic with the conjectured constant is established for any k ≥ 3, unconditionally. AI search: no source names an AI system in any moments result. Every AI-involved zeta item I found in the window concerns zeros or zero-free regions: Anthropic’s unreleased Claude research version (post dated 10 Aug 2026, zeros from 41.6% to 67.2%), the Alpöge–Furman arXiv paper (13 Aug 2026, credited to Claude in its comments), Lamzouri’s paper (2 Sep 2026, which credits the earlier Claude proof but whose own argument is human), and the zeta zero-free regions in OpenAI’s 722-manuscript release (6 Oct 2026, family 003 and a 11/12 companion). I scanned every family title and summary in OpenAI’s raw CONTENTS.md (families 001–377, with gaps at 045, 061, 070, 123, 163 and a truncated first chunk boundary) for zeta, Riemann, moments, L-functions, Dirichlet, Hecke, random-matrix and Keating/Snaith terms and found no moments entry; the only matches were the zero-free and quasi-Riemann families, and a ‘Patterson’s first moment for cubic Gauss sums’ title, which is not a zeta moment. The Wikipedia list of AI mathematical discoveries contains one zeta entry (the Claude zeros result). The Gemini case-study paper (arXiv 2602.03837) names no zeta topic in its abstract; its case list was not in what I could read. Quotes: where a page would not return text verbatim, the quoted sentences are as returned by a summarising tool and are marked as such in the relevant fields; they should be checked against the primary text before being relied on. Close calls: whether Page’s and Durkan–Page’s lower bounds count, whether the Ng–Shen–Wong conditional asymptotic counts for k = 4 (the constant matches; the hypothesis is conditional), and whether the bullet means the integral at a fixed k or the conjectured order for all k.
competing_reading: Reading A: the Keating–Snaith asymptotic is open for every k ≥ 3, since no unconditional asymptotic with the conjectured constant is posted; Durkan–Page and Page are partial lower bounds, and Ng 2016 and Ng–Shen–Wong are conditional, so the bullet has no unconditional resolution for any k in its family. Reading B: the bullet asks only that the integral grows at the conjectured order T(log T)^{k²}; on that reading Durkan–Page’s Theorem 1 (k = 3) and Theorem 10 (k = 5 to 11) establish the order for those k unconditionally, and the bullet is partly settled for them, while the constant is still open. A third reading takes the Ng–Shen–Wong result (conditional on RH and Conjecture 1, with the Keating–Snaith constant) as a resolution for k = 4 that depends on an unproven hypothesis the authors say has no numerical confirmation; on that reading the k = 4 case is conditionally settled and the judging pass must decide whether conditional asymptotics count.
what_would_settle_it: An unconditional asymptotic for ∫_0^T|ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k}dt with the Keating–Snaith constant for any k ≥ 3 (or the removal of the gap 34.4 → 42 in Durkan–Page); a proof of the quaternary additive divisor conjecture (which would make Ng–Shen–Wong unconditional); the first posting and full text of Page’s J. Number Theory 280 (2026) paper, with its constants and date (to place it before or after 26 January 2024); a check by independent experts of Durkan–Page’s Theorem 1 and Theorem 10 constants; and the Keating–Snaith original text (CMP 2000) to confirm the stated normalisation for real k.

event.what_happened: Benjamin Durkan, Neea Palojärvi and Tim Trudgian, ‘The error term of the fourth moment of the Riemann zeta-function’, arXiv 2506.16766, first submitted 20 June 2025. They reduce the powers of log T in the known bounds for the error term E_2(T) of the fourth moment, and in the integral of E_2(t)² over [0,T], and obtain logarithmic improvements in upper bounds for ∫|ζ|^{2k} for 8 ≤ k ≤ 12; the explicit example stated is ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^{12} dt ≪ T²(log T)^{15}.
event.revisions: v2 revised 4 Oct 2026 (per tool reading of the listing).
event.delivers: Upper bounds only: improved log powers in the error term for k = 2 and in upper bounds for 2k = 8 to 12 (e.g. the 12th power ≪ T²(log T)^{15}). The power of T (T²) is far from the conjectured order T(log T)^{k²}, which for 2k = 12 gives exponent 36. No asymptotic is stated for any k ≥ 3, and the abstract read does not say whether the bounds are unconditional.
event.remains: The asymptotic for k ≥ 3; the correct order of magnitude for the moments in question.
event.direction: Upper bounds with improved logarithms that do not reach the conjectured order in T; neutral for the asymptotic.

judgement.why: The statement asks for the asymptotics of the moment integral across all k, so k=1 and k=2 (Hardy–Littlewood, Ingham, Heath-Brown) are pre-snapshot cases. Conditional asymptotics (Ng; Ng–Shen–Wong) and the RH-conditional Harper bound settle a changed question with an added hypothesis, so I scored them variant; this was the closest call, against reading them as cases. The unconditional lower bounds of the conjectured order (Durkan–Page, Page JNT) and the improved upper bounds (Durkan–Palojärvi–Trudgian) move quantities on the actual integral and leave the constant open, so they are bound. Arguin–Creighton gives a new proof of known fractional-moment bounds, which moves nothing: none. Derivative moments, L-function families, zeta sums, the amplified fourth moment and all zeros/zero-free-region items (including the AI ones) are variants. I gave their AI roles from their own quotes, but they do not bear on this problem.
judgement.doubts: Page JNT 280 (2026) could not be dated relative to the snapshot, so after_snapshot is null. Its verification rests on a journal citation the researcher did not check. Whether conditional asymptotics should count as cases is a policy question; I treated them as variants. The Durkan–Page Theorem 10 range was read through a garbled source.
